Global (All).title: North Korea: Kim Jong-un's sister hints at nuclear tests
Global (All).summary: North Korea's sister of leader Kim Jong-un has hinted that the country could stage a nuclear test in the near future, in a speech in which she also praised the "unforgettable feat" achieved by her brother's "invincible people's army".

Global (All).title: China's Xi Jinping extends tenure as Communist Party leader
Global (All).summary: China's president Xi Jinping has extended his tenure as leader of the country's ruling Communist Party, securing a historic third term and setting him up to rule as president for life.

Global (All).title: Taiwan: Chinese warplanes fly near island as US official visits
Global (All).summary: Chinese warplanes have flown near Taiwan as a US official visited the island, amid growing tensions between Taipei and Beijing.

United States.title: US Congress Passes Bill to Restrict TikTok's Operations
United States.summary: The US Congress has passed a bill aimed at restricting TikTok's operations in the country, citing national security concerns.

United States.title: Gun violence in Chicago leaves multiple injured or dead
United States.summary: A series of gun violence incidents in Chicago have left multiple individuals injured or dead, sparking concerns about public safety.

United States.title: Twitter Suspends Accounts of Chinese Diplomats After US Warns
United States.summary: Twitter has suspended the accounts of several Chinese diplomats after the US government warned the company to take action against suspected bot accounts.

South Korea.summary: Protests against military conscription reform in South Korea: Amidst ongoing protests, South Korean authorities arrested 11 activists for allegedly planning mass disruptions.

Rallies against COVID-19 vaccination mandates in South Korea see significant turnout: Anti-vaccine mandate protests across the nation have heightened political tensions, with authorities imposing new restrictions.

Seoul city council passes bill to strengthen whistleblower protection laws: In a bid to bolster trust in government, Seoul's municipal assembly passed a bill aimed at shielding public servants and other employees from retaliation for reporting wrongdoing.

Japan.title: Japan's Fugitive Former Defence Official Arrested on Suspicion of Leaking Secrets
Japan.summary: Japanese authorities arrested a former defense ministry official who has been on the run for a week on suspicion of leaking classified information, as the government grapples with a series of high-profile security breaches.

Japan.title: Japan's opposition to consider no-confidence motion against government over corruption
Japan.summary: Japan's main opposition party said it would consider a no-confidence motion against the government over corruption scandals, in a move that could potentially topple Prime Minister Fumio Kishida's administration.

Japan.title: Japan's Fukuoka region issues evacuation advisory for 140,000 residents amid heavy rain
Japan.summary: Japanese authorities issued an evacuation advisory for around 140,000 residents in the Fukuoka region on Wednesday, as heavy rain battered the area.
